# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 80 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 80 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_080_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Chapter 3

**1** He showed me many other trees, some budding and some withered. **2** And he said to me, "Do you see these trees?" "I see them, Lord," I replied. "Those that are budding and sprouting," he said, "are those who are about to repent and live; for the Lord, seeing their repentance, judged it good to grant life to them. **3** But those that are withered and bear no fruit are those who have apostatized in their hearts and will not return to repentance, nor return among the living." **4** I said to him, "Lord, why then did you bring some of the withered ones among those who repented?" He answered, "So that, beholding the joyful appearance of those who are repenting, they might be put to shame and themselves repent. For if they see the glory of those who repented — and knew not the Lord before, but now know him — they will repent with all their heart." **5** "But if they do not repent, Lord," I said, "what will become of them?" "They shall die," he said — those who do not repent at that point. But those who repented and lived righteously shall live unto God. But those who did not repent and persisted in their wicked deeds shall die." **6** I asked, "Those who returned the rod entirely green and cracked — who are they?" He said to me, "They were always faithful and good, but they harbored jealousy toward one another over questions of pre-eminence and glory. They are all foolish to have jealousy among themselves over pre-eminence." **7** "And those who returned rods half-withered and cracked — who are these?" **8** "These are those who were faithful but became rich and gained standing among the Gentiles. They clothed themselves in great pride and became arrogant, and abandoned the truth, and did not attach themselves to the righteous but lived with the Gentiles, and this way seemed better to them. Yet they did not depart from God but remained in the faith, though they did not perform the works of faith. **9** Many of them repented, but some continued in their deeds. These received their rods retaining sap, for they did not depart from the living God, nor did the name depart from their lips. Therefore they received their rods with sap remaining."

---

### Translator's Note
The socioeconomic concern in vv. 8-9 is one of Hermas's most distinctive prophetic notes: wealthy Christians who assimilate into Gentile social networks, maintaining nominal faith while abandoning its practice. This is the "double-minded" (dipsuchos) danger Hermas returns to repeatedly. SOPHIA follows LOGOS formally; PNEUMA's "another chance at life" in v. 2 is paraphrastic but captures the pastoral tone.
